core_obligations: The canonical maps (proof lines 4229-4237): the author defines each map as the adjoint of the identity, so that it is the counit of the corresponding adjunction.
The cocycle condition (proof lines 4238-4242): the compatibility of these counits under composition follows from the general result on composing counits.

The isomorphism (proof lines 4243-4263): the map from the colimit to the sheaf is shown to be an isomorphism by evaluating at an object, where the companion result describes the value of the sheaf as a filtered colimit whose terms agree with the values of the pushforwards appearing in the colimit in the statement.
proof_roadmap: Define the canonical maps as counits of the adjunctions.
Use the composition rule for counits for the cocycle condition.
Evaluate at an object and compare with the description of the values of the sheaf.
difficulty_reason: The lemma expresses a sheaf on the colimit site as the filtered colimit of the pullbacks of its pushforwards along the transition morphisms, with transition maps satisfying a cocycle condition (statement lines 4214-4226). The proof is a complete argument: the canonical maps are defined as counits of the adjunctions (proof lines 4229-4237); the cocycle condition follows from the general composition rule for counits (proof lines 4238-4242); and the identification of the colimit with the sheaf is obtained by evaluating at an object and comparing with the description of the values supplied by the companion result (proof lines 4243-4263). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two colimit descriptions. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
